Overview of Microsoft Agent 365
Feedback
Summarize this article for me
AI agents are quickly becoming part of everyday work. Microsoft Agent 365 is the observability platform for AI. It gives you one view of the agents in your organization, including agents from Microsoft and from other companies. Your IT, security, and business teams see the same information, each in the tools they already use.
Agent 365 is built on four pillars:
management
,
governance
,
security
, and
business value
.
Management
Management helps you see and run all your agents from one place.
The agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center lists the agents in your organization. It includes agents from Microsoft, from partners, and from your own teams. For each agent, you can see who owns it, how much people use it, and whether it has any risks.
You can also bring in agents that you built on other platforms. Agent Map shows your agents on a visual map, grouped by the platform you built them on. It helps you quickly spot the agents that need attention.
Learn more:
Agent registry
,
Agent map
,
Connected platforms
.
Governance
Governance helps you make sure every agent has an owner, only the access it needs, and a record of what it does.
You review and approve agents before you publish them to your organization, and you decide who can use them. When an agent loses its owner, you can find it and assign a new one.
You control which tools agents can connect to. You can also apply a standard set of policies to each new agent. Microsoft Purview keeps a record of agent activity, so you're ready for audits.
Learn more:
Agent management overview
,
Policy templates
.
Security
Security helps you find risky agents, control what they can do, and keep them protected.
The agent registry shows risk signals from Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Purview in one place. You can see which agents need attention first.
Microsoft Entra controls what each agent can access. Microsoft Purview helps stop agents from oversharing or leaking sensitive data. Microsoft Defender watches for threats and blocks unsafe or harmful activity.
If an agent looks risky, you can block it right away while your security team investigates.
Learn more:
Use Microsoft Purview for data security and compliance
,
Enable security for AI agents using Microsoft Defender
.
Business value
Business value helps you see what you spend on AI and what you get back.
The Agent overview page in the Microsoft 365 admin center shows how many people use agents and how many hours agents run.
Cost management shows how many Copilot Credits your organization uses, broken down by user, group, agent, and service. Copilot Credits are the units your AI usage is billed in. You can set spending limits for groups and users, and see who is getting close to their limit.
These views help you see where AI is used most and decide where to invest next.
Learn more:
Monitor Copilot Credit spending
.
Agent 365 availability and prerequisites
Microsoft Agent 365 is generally available for the Commercial segment on a per user basis. For more information about the product, see
Microsoft Agent 365, now generally available, expands capabilities and integrations
. At launch, a set of
partner agents
are available to deploy directly from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Microsoft Agent 365 works best when using Microsoft E5 as a pre-requisite. At least one user must be licensed with a
qualifying Microsoft Agent 365 license
to enable Agent 365.
Plans and licensing
For plans and pricing information, see
Microsoft Agent 365: The Control Plane for Agents
. For details on feature availability by plan, see the
Microsoft Agent 365 service description
.
Microsoft Agent 365 is licensed on a per-user basis. For details, see
Microsoft Agent 365 Licensing FAQs
.
